LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.

MATERIALS
•	 Crayons or pencils
In this activity, the Ss will have to follow the path and give 
directions to their classmates. While doing so, they have to 
follow the routes with their fingers.
Then when they get to their destination, they should circle 
the shop/place using a crayon. Do the first one as an example 
and then choose Ss to play the teacher’s role. Always encourage 
them to use full structures. The target language is as follows, 
but the Ss’ statements may vary:
Route 1
“You are at the bookshop. When you exit the bookshop turn 
right, then go straight ahead, go past the supermarket and the 
sports centre. When you get to the sports centre, turn left. Go 
past the charity shop and then turn right, go straight ahead 
and go past the pet shop and the town hall. The place you 
are going to is opposite the football pitch. What place is it?”
Route 2
“You are at the bakery. When you exit the bakery turn left 
and go straight ahead, past the greengrocer’s, thecharity shop, 
the pet shop, the town hall and the football pitch. When you 
get to the library, turn right, go straight ahead and past the

bank. The place you are going to is next to the gym. What 
place is it?”
Route 3
“You are at the ice cream parlour. When you exit the ice 
cream parlour turn right. Go straight ahead and when you 
get to the toyshop, turn left. Go straight ahead and, at the 
pet shop, turn right. Then, go straight ahead and go past the 
charity shop and the clothes shop. The place you are going 
to is opposite the newsagent’s. What place is it?”
Route 4
“You are at the library. When you exit the library, turn left. 
Go straight ahead, past the football pitch. When you get to the 
town hall, turn right. Then go straight ahead and go past the 
animal shelter. Then, when you get to the petrol station, turn 
left. Go straight ahead, past the café and the hospital. The 
shop you are going to is behind the school. What shop is it?”

5.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (15’)
P.E.M.4.1

P.E.M.4

Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet.
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and do 
the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
6.– ACTIVITY 4: FOLLOWING DIRECTIONS (3’)
> Warm-Up
Put a red sticker on each Ss’ left hand and a green one on 
their right. Then practise left, right and straight ahead by using 
your hands. Say, “Turn left!” and have everybody turn to the left 
(you should too; having your back turned to your Ss is helpful, 
so everybody is pointing to the same left). Do the same with 
right and straight ahead.
Gradually say each command faster and faster.
> Main Activity
Next, the Ss should form a line. When you say, “Go straight 
ahead”, they must pat the person in front of them on the head. If 
you say, “Turn left” Ss must pat the left shoulder of the person 
in front of them and if you say, “Turn right”, their right shoulder. 
Finally, get them (still in a line) to follow your instructions 
but walking around the class pretending to be on a train.

> Advanced Groups
If your Ss have understood the concepts quickly, you can 
let them take on the teacher role and give commands to their 
classmates.
7.– ACTIVITY 1: CHARACTER MATCHING (8’)
P.2.1
P.2.1
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the actions that each character is doing by 
putting the Place cards (P.2.1) down on the table. Say, “Grandpa 
and Grandma are going to the doctor’s, Mum is going to the 
hairdresser’s, and Dad is doing the gardening.”
Show the Ss the X cards and ask, “Why can’t Mum take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop?”, to which they should reply, 
“Because she is going to the hairdresser’s.” Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the pairs.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
To introduce the activity, say, “Let’s see if you remember 
what Pam and Paul’s family are doing!”. Put the P.2.1 cards 
in two piles face down: X cards on one side, Place cards on 
the other. The Ss must flip a card from each pile to match the 
character with the correct reason for them to not be able to 
take Pam and Paul to the toyshop.
If they have a match, they should say, “Mum can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop, because she is going to the 
hairdresser’s. I’ve got a pair!” If they don’t, they should say 
“I’ve got Grandpa and Grandma and doing the gardening; it’s 
not a pair, what a shame!”
> Correct matches and structures
•	 Mum + going to the hairdresser’s: “Mum (she) can’t take 
Pam and Paul to the toyshop because she is going to 
the hairdresser’s.”

•	 Dad + doing the gardening: “Dad (he) can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop because he is doing the gardening.” 
•	 Grandma and Grandpa + going to the doctor’s: “Grandma 
and Grandpa (they) can’t take Pam and Paul to the 
toyshop because they are going to the doctor’s.” 
> Follow-Up
Quickly split the group into two teams. Show team A the X 
card and team B the matching place card. Each team should 
say the part of the structure corresponding to their card. For 
example:
•	 Team A: “Grandpa and Grandma can’t take Pam and 
Paul to the toyshop...”
•	 Team B: “...because they are going to the doctor’s.”

BONUS
ACTIVITY 3: CAN YOU TELL ME THE WAY?
P.2.3
P.2.3
TARGET LANGUAGE
Turn right
Go past
Go straight ahead
Turn left
Behind
On your right
On your left
Opposite
Next to
Between
> How to Play
In this game, the Ss must tell their classmate the correct 
way to get to the shop to buy a certain item.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the name of the items (P.2.3) with the Ss 
and where they can buy them. Ask, “Where can you buy a 
dress?” to which they should answer, “You can buy a dress at 
the clothes shop.” If needed, review the shops on the A3 that 
your Ss find tricky (such as charity shop, town hall, dentist, 
basketball court, football pitch, etc.)
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Pair the Ss up (S1 and S2). Put the Item memory cards (P.2.3) 
face down on the table. To do the activity, proceed as detailed 
below. We highly encourage you to model the steps with a S 
first. Say, “Let’s go explore the city!”. Then proceed as follows: 
•	 S1: Takes a bike cutout and turns over an item card.
•	 T: “What do you need to buy?”
•	 S1: “I need to buy dog food.” (or whatever item is on 
the card). 
•	 T: “Where can you buy dog food?”
•	 S2: “You can buy dog food at the pet shop.”
•	 T: “S1, you are at the bookshop.”

•	 S1: “Can you tell me the way (to the pet shop), please?”
•	 S2: Gives directions accordingly. For example: “To get 
to the pet shop, turn right. Go straight ahead and go 
past the supermarket and the sports centre. At the 
sports centre turn left. You will find the pet shop on 
your right / the pet shop is opposite the charity shop.”
> Follow-Up
Ask Ss about the location of different shops. For example: 
“John, where is the greengrocer’s?” to which they should reply, 
“The greengrocer’s is between the bakery and the charity 
shop.”
ACTIVITY 7: DIRECTIONS SONG (TR#13)
> Main Activity
To perform the song, have the Ss stand with their back against 
the wall in a line, side by side. Then the first time they sing the 
song they will simply turn left and right while standing in place 
and then walk straight ahead when the song says to do so.
The second time you do the activity, they must line up behind 
one another forming a train, holding onto the shoulders of the 
S in front of them. Then, this time, when the song says turn left 
and right, they will actually walk around the room while doing 
so. The song will speed up so make sure the Ss are ready to 
do the actions quickly.
DIRECTIONS SONG
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
That was great! Now line up! Ready? Steady? Go! 
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat) 
Very good! Now let’s go faster!
Turn left, left, left
Turn right, right, right
Walk straight ahead
Straight, straight, straight
(repeat)
